requiredFindings.claim: The preamble, item 24's heading, item 24's forbidden substitutes, and the global admission substitute still require a manifest-class refusal to happen before any ExecutionId is drawn or reserved. On the first-use route the creation prelude's ExecutionId is already reserved when R10a runs, and item 24's decision paragraph and D4-T1 require the refusal to proceed with that reservation left in place.
requiredFindings.evidence: Line 9 assigns items 24 and 25 the property 'refused before any ExecutionId is drawn or reserved'. Item 25's placement at R1 is before mint_intent (PROPOSAL.md:738, J1:300), so that absolute wording is true for item 25. Item 24 is the manifest-class row. Its heading (line 696) is 'Manifest-class refusals before any ExecutionId is drawn'. Its forbidden substitutes (line 730) include 'an ExecutionId drawn or reserved before these checks'. The global admission substitute, rewritten in r2 (line 1168), forbids 'an excluded form admitted silently, or refused after an ExecutionId is drawn or reserved'. Accepted J1 r3 draws and reserves the creation prelude's ExecutionId in mint_intent, before P0, and that id names the creation act only (J1:161, J1:172). R10a is after that draw on the first-use route. Item 24's own decision says so: a refusal at R10a draws and reserves no analysis-attempt ExecutionId, and on first use the prelude's id was drawn earlier and is not the analysis attempt's (PROPOSAL.md:710). D4-T1 asserts the same state: after the refusal, ExecutionIdReservations equals its set at R10a's entry, empty or the prelude's alone (PROPOSAL.md:732). REG:374 and QG:588 require admission-time excluded forms to be refused with no ExecutionId. The decision paragraph reads that as no analysis-attempt id. The four absolute sentences read it as no id of any kind, so the lawful first-use refusal is a forbidden substitute. R10a between R10 and R11/R12 (J1:309-311), the ephemeral placement before the ephemeral draw, and SD-6 as a separately reviewed amendment to accepted J1 are the sound half of the r1 answer.
requiredFindings.fix: State the prohibition as no analysis-attempt ExecutionId. Keep the creation prelude's reservation as the exception the decision paragraph and D4-T1 already state. Apply that wording in the preamble (line 9), in item 24's heading (line 696), in item 24's forbidden substitutes (line 730), and in the global admission substitute (line 1168). Leave item 25 absolute: R1 is before any draw. Leave R10a where it is. Do not bind the prelude id to the analysis attempt.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: D5-T2c asserts tree: incomplete for an injected proc_listpids failure and for a group member held past the reap ceiling, and it asserts that killpg EPERM is never read as empty. The Guaranteed cell and the escalation sentence also give the root exit: unreaped when the root itself is still alive at that ceiling. D5-T2c does not assert that root case. The cells already agree with the escalation sentence. Adding the root case to the control would close the list.

Item 6 states that /var/tmp is on disk on both distributions. LX-5 says /var/tmp and the fs.protected_* values are not in CF-P, and the LX header says no row is established until a Linux lane runs it. The move off AL2023's /tmp matches CFP:282, which measured that /tmp as a tmpfs limited to half of RAM. Marking item 6's disk sentence as desk-checked and unmeasured would match LX-5.

D4-T1's registry bullet is the proof that covers the durable path, the first-use path, and the ephemeral path: after the refusal the reservation set equals the set at R10a's entry. The census bullet, x3d.session.execution-draw never reached, observes the durable session draw. J1:179 names that census point, and J1:428 places it right after the handoff, which is CommitSession::open. The ephemeral and render draws are not that point (J1:163-164, J1:174). The registry bullet already covers them.

priorFindings.evidence: The macOS Guaranteed cell now promises that SIGKILL is sent to every group member at each group kill, that no signal goes to a recycled group id, and that the record is truthful: tree: group-killed only when proc_listpids(PROC_PGRP_ONLY) lists the zombie root alone, otherwise tree: incomplete (PROPOSAL.md:537, :543). A root or member still alive at the reap ceiling is outside that cell; the root takes exit: unreaped and a member takes tree: incomplete (PROPOSAL.md:543, :548). The snapshot is a recursive proc_listchildpids walk that retries when the returned count fills the buffer (PROPOSAL.md:534; SDK27 libproc.h:95; CFP:224). Not guaranteed (b) is the in-group fork-and-setsid window between the snapshot and the group SIGKILL (PROPOSAL.md:545). D5-T2 expects best effort only (CFP:229). D5-T2b expects the window's child to survive on macOS. D5-T2c covers a failed confirm, a member held past the ceiling, and killpg EPERM (CFP:228). A group SIGSTOP is rejected as unmeasured. The root-alive control gap is NBO-1, not a reopening of the cell.

closure-recheck-failed is host-side and pre-spawn, and it takes J1 r3 row 28: operational-failed 4, HOST.IO_FAILURE, host-io, DELIVERY.CLOSURE_BYTES_CORRUPT (PROPOSAL.md:656, :764; WS:1375; J1:643). spawn-failed stays on that row with DELIVERY.CLOSURE_UNSPAWNABLE (PROPOSAL.md:657). session-spec-inconsistent takes NE:3573's host-invariant route, which the law spells as J1 r3 row 2's route: operational-failed 4, SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE, host-invariant, detail absent (PROPOSAL.md:658; J1:617). Provider-spoken mismatches stay control-refusal or provider-protocol on row 30 (PROPOSAL.md:23, :778; NE:3529; J1:645). The same split is in the cause list (PROPOSAL.md:388) and in D4-T3.

revoked is revocation during the operation: request-rejected 2, EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED, TRUST.COMPONENT_REVOKED_DURING_OPERATION (PROPOSAL.md:659; SL:1306; X4:120; J1:633). observer-fail-stop is operational-failed 4, HOST.IO_FAILURE, host-io, OBSERVER.FAIL_STOP (PROPOSAL.md:660, :587; SL:1311; X4:121; J1:634). Both keep the S6 kill ladder (PROPOSAL.md:24). The cause list withdraws the shared revoked (PROPOSAL.md:388).

Manifest-class refusals moved out of C4a to R10a, after R10's trust read and before R11 and R12 (PROPOSAL.md:705; J1:309-311). The decision paragraph distinguishes the analysis-attempt id from the creation prelude's id (PROPOSAL.md:700-710; J1:161-174). D4-T1 asserts registry equality, including the prelude-only set on first use (PROPOSAL.md:732). Item 26 is post-draw and pre-stage (PROPOSAL.md:9). Item 25 stays at R1. SD-6 is a separately reviewed amendment to accepted J1, and D4 waits for it (PROPOSAL.md:1080, :1121). The absolute sentences at lines 9, 696, 730, and 1168 still forbid the first-use refusal those paragraphs require. That remainder is this round's RF-1.

F-8's Linux table now runs LX-1 through LX-22. LX-15 is PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and the layer order. LX-16 is the seccomp filter-mode probe. LX-17 through LX-22 cover Landlock EXECUTE, io_uring, signal-target filtering, pipe2 and glibc's exec-failure report, wait4 units, and flock release. The header says no row is established, and none is passed, until a Linux lane runs it (PROPOSAL.md:1019). LX-15 and LX-16 are marked partly, with the Landlock half, inheritance, order, and the probe calls not in CF-P. LX-17 through LX-22 are marked not in CF-P. F-1, F-2, F-4, and the ordinary Linux citations point at these rows. glibc 2.39's EINVAL fallback is in the CF-P record; the law relies on the 2.34 ENOSYS fallback (LX-14).
